title: Intentional Rhythm Retro Playbook
content:
Purpose: keep a small, repeatable retro+planning routine that lives between weekly check-ins and quarterly OKRs. This is my lightweight playbook — half notebook, half experiment log. Not polished. Notes-to-self throughout.

How I want this to behave (hypothesis):
- 20–30 minute end-of-week retro that surfaces 2 wins, 2 frictions, 1 idea to try next week.
- Capture one metric snapshot (hard number) and one qualitative signal (short sentence).
- Run 1 micro-experiment every two weeks to move a specific metric (not more than one at a time).
- After 6 experiments, decide whether pattern emerges and adjust quarterly objective.

Weekly template (copy this into week note):
- Week: YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD
- Metric snapshot (primary): e.g., "feature adoption = 12% DAU -> 14%" (hard number)
- Qual signal: e.g., "support tickets mention confusions about 'session restore' twice"
- 2 wins (short): 
  - Win 1: shipped partial rollout for quick-ack flow (observed +3% completion)
  - Win 2: cleared inbox of old action items; freed 4 hours to focus
- 2 frictions (short): 
  - Friction 1: latency regression on nightly runs, investigate infra config
  - Friction 2: prompts drift in evals, quality dip on long-tail prompts
- One experiment to try next week (name + brief plan + success criteria):
  - Example: "KV-cache-tweak-ttl" -> change TTL from 30s to 90s for non-interactive routes; success = 5% cost reduction without >=1% latency p95 increase
- Quick TODOs for next week (3-5 items, prioritized)
- Retro note (one sentence): what felt different this week?

Quarterly OKR sketch (working draft):
- Objective: Keep inference cost per 1M tokens flat while improving median latency for interactive apps.
  - KR1: reduce average per-token GPU cost by 12% versus baseline (measure = $/1M tokens).
  - KR2: median interactive latency <= 110ms p50 for 90% of routes (measure by route dashboard).
  - KR3: roll out KV-prefix cache to 3 prod routes, observe no regressions in quality evals.

Personal KPI ledger (short):
- Primary metric (monthly): tangible wins that support product OKR. Current baseline: $/1M tokens = $420 (Nov baseline).
- Secondary metric (weekly): number of blocked customer threads resolved within 48h (target >= 90%). Current: 76%.
- Learning metric: experiments run / quarter. Target = 6.

Micro-experiment log (format: name | date start | hypothesis | measurement | outcome):
- kv-cache-ttl-90s | 2026-01-04 | longer TTL reduces token compute and costs without hurting p95 latency | measurement: cost / token, p95 latency | outcome: partial — cost down 4%, p95 +0.8% (within threshold) -> promote to A/B on more routes
- prompt-sanity-check | 2026-01-18 | adding a short quality prefilter reduces hallucination rate on set-of-100 prompts | measurement: hallucination rate on evals | outcome: failed (no measurable change), hypothesis revised

Retro patterns I'm tracking (signal bank):
- Recurring blockers: infra config drift after autoscaler updates; action: add weekly autoscaler sanity check (10m).
- Time sinks: debugging low-signal flakes; experiment: dedicate one 'quiet debugging hour' per week and log outcomes.
- Energy pattern: highest focus Tue–Thu mornings; schedule deep work then.

Rules of the playbook (constraints):
- Never run more than one 'cost-impact' experiment at a time. If multiple ideas stack up, queue them.
- Keep experiments scoped to 1 week of data typically, at most 3 weeks for noisy signals.
- Metric thresholds must be defined before experiment start (avoid moving goalposts).
- If an experiment yields ambiguous result, run a variant (A/B or more routes) rather than toss it out.

Personal retrospective, Feb 2026 (raw notes):
- Feb wins: stabilized KV cache on two routes, trimmed 7% off token usage on background jobs; cadence of retros improved (actually did them).
- Feb misses: stalled on the latency p50 target because an infra upgrade introduced variability; too many open threads left me reactive.
- Key insight: small scope wins (background jobs, batch caching) compound; prioritize those before touching interactive tail latencies.
- Commitment for March: run one focused experiment to harden autoscaler configs + create 'blocking dashboard' with top 5 items that stop weekly progress.

Open questions / TODOs (short laundry list):
- TODO: schedule 30m sync with SRE (Marcus Hsu) to walk autoscaler rollouts (Jira PRD-4122).
- TODO: convert the weekly template into a tiny Google Doc template and link it in personal shortcuts.
- Question: do I keep the "one experiment at a time" rule if an experiment is very low-risk? (note: probably yes, stick to discipline)
- TODO: push summary of the best experiment (kv-cache-ttl-90s) to the 'personal-playbook' repo README.

Quick heuristics (short checklist when writing an experiment):
- Can I measure it with an existing metric pipeline? If not, build minimal signal first.
- Does it change cost or quality? Tag accordingly (cost/quality/ops).
- How long until I can make a go/no-go call? Put that in the plan.

Final note: this is intentionally messy. The goal is to make the rhythm so small and useful I keep doing it. Next step: copy the weekly template into a doc and start week-of-2026-03-01.
